title: Burr King Disc Grinder Shaft - Combined Bending, Torsion, and Deflection
studentDocumentTitle: Student Packet - Burr King Disc Grinder Shaft
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Burr King Disc Grinder Shaft
summary: Size an equivalent local overhung grinder spindle from a transverse-deflection criterion and evaluate its combined bending and torsional stress state.
imageAttribution: Professor-supplied Burr King Model 20 context image. It is used only for physical context; no shaft geometry, bearing spacing, force, or serviceability limit is inferred from it.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference showing the equivalent local overhung solid circular shaft under transverse force and transmitted torque.
problemStatement:
Analyze the horizontal disc spindle/shaft using an instructor-assigned local overhung solid-circular cantilever idealization. The actual bearing-supported spindle is not claimed to be a literal bare cantilever.

Use the assigned power and speed to determine torque, the assigned transverse force and effective overhang to determine bending, and the assigned modulus and deflection criterion to calculate the theoretical minimum diameter.
engineeringGoal: Determine the stiffness-sized theoretical shaft diameter, calculate bending, torsional, and von Mises stresses at that diameter, evaluate force and overhang sensitivities, and state a limited assessment without claiming an actual Burr King shaft size, safety factor, or certification.
